content.text:
For any change made in the **prod** namespace—whether it’s a rollback, a forward rollout, or scaling the number of replicas—our policy requires a **change-ticket** that is open in the help-desk system.  

**What the ticket must contain**

| Requirement | Details |
|-------------|---------|
| **Ticket ID** | A valid help-desk ticket reference in the format `HD-\d+` (e.g., `HD-12345`). The ticket must be **open** at the time the change is applied. |
| **Ticket content** | The ticket should describe the intended change (e.g., “Roll back payments deployment to revision 12”, “Scale payments from 3 → 5 replicas”). Include the revision number (for rollbacks) or the new replica count (for scaling). |
| **Approval** | The ticket must be approved by the appropriate change-management authority (usually the SOC/Compliance team) before the operation can proceed. |
| **Audit trail** | After the change, the system records the ticket ID, the user who initiated the change, and the exact command executed, which becomes part of the SOC 2 audit log. |

**Why this matters**

- **Accountability:** The ticket links the change to a specific request and approver, satisfying the “who did what and when” principle.
- **Risk mitigation:** Reviewing the ticket ensures that the change has been vetted for impact, rollback plan, and compliance with policy.
- **Auditability:** The ticket ID is captured in the audit log, making it easy to trace the change back to the request.

**If you’re just documenting the requirement for your audit notes, you can state:**

> “All changes in the production namespace must be initiated through an open help-desk change ticket (ID `HD-\d+`). The ticket must describe the operation (roll-back to a specific revision or new replica count), be approved by the designated change-management authority, and the system will record the ticket ID, initiator, and execution details in the audit log.”

Let me know if you need any specific ticket IDs or further clarification!

content.text:
Before any change can be made in the **prod** namespace—whether it’s a rollback, a forward rollout, or a scaling operation—the following items must be in place:

| Requirement | What it means | Why it’s needed |
|-------------|---------------|-----------------|
| **Change-ticket ID** | A valid, open help-desk ticket whose ID matches the pattern `HD-\d+` (e.g., `HD-12345`). | Provides auditability, accountability, and traceability for every production-modifying action. |
| **Authorization** | The requester must have the proper clearance/role to perform the change (typically a security or ops team member). | Ensures only authorized personnel can alter production services. |
| **Risk assessment / impact analysis** | Documented analysis of how the change will affect service availability, data integrity, and other business-critical processes. | Helps mitigate unexpected downtime or regressions. |
| **Rollback plan** (for rollbacks) | A documented procedure that specifies the exact revision to roll back to, the expected outcome, and the steps to verify success. | Guarantees a quick way back to a known-good state if the change causes issues. |
| **Testing / verification** (for forward changes) | Unit, integration, or staging tests confirming the change works as intended before it reaches production. | Reduces the chance of introducing bugs. |
| **Communication plan** | Notification to stakeholders (e.g., product owners, support teams, customers) about the change schedule and expected impact. | Keeps everyone informed and allows pre-emptive mitigation. |
| **Post-change review** | A follow-up audit or monitoring period after the change is deployed, documenting results and any incidents. | Ensures compliance with SOC 2 “control” evidence and provides a record of effectiveness. |

**In short:** Any production-modifying operation (rollout, rollback, scaling, etc.) must be tied to an open help-desk ticket (`HD-\d+`), be authorized, accompanied by a documented risk/impact analysis, a rollback procedure (if applicable), pre-change testing, stakeholder communication, and a post-change review.  

Since you only need the checklist for audit notes and not to perform any actual change, you can reference the above items directly in your SOC 2 documentation. Let me know if you need a template or further detail on any specific item.

content.text:
For any change that touches a production environment—whether it’s a rollback, a forward rollout, or scaling the number of replicas—our policy requires a **change ticket** (the ID of an open help-desk ticket) to be on file before the operation can be applied.

**What the ticket must contain**

| Requirement | Details |
|-------------|---------|
| **Ticket type** | Must be a help-desk ticket (e.g., a support request, incident ticket, or change-request ticket) that authorizes the change. |
| **Ticket ID format** | `HD-\d+` (e.g., `HD-12345`). The system validates the pattern when the change is processed. |
| **Content** | The ticket should describe the change (what will be done, why it’s needed, and who approved it). It’s the audit trail that proves the change was authorized. |
| **Status** | The ticket must be **open** at the time the change is executed; a closed or archived ticket will cause the operation to fail. |
| **Assignee / Owner** | The ticket should be assigned to the person or team responsible for the change, and the owner’s name/ID should be recorded in the ticket metadata. |
| **Review & Approval** | In most SOC 2 frameworks the ticket must be reviewed and approved by the appropriate governance or change-management board before it’s marked “ready” for execution. |
| **Retention** | After the change is made, the ticket (including its history and approval notes) must be retained for the duration of the audit period (typically 6-12 months, depending on your policy). |

**Why this matters for SOC 2**

- **Accountability** – The ticket proves who requested and approved the change.
- **Auditability** – It provides a clear, immutable record of the change’s purpose, impact, and approval.
- **Risk Management** – It ensures that changes are not made impulsively; they’re vetted and documented.
- **Compliance** – Many SOC 2 sub-requirements (e.g., “processes for change management”) explicitly require a documented change request.

**If you’re just documenting the requirement** (no actual change is being made), you can note in your audit notes:

> “All production changes (rollbacks, forward rolls, scaling) must be initiated only after an open help-desk change ticket (ID `HD-\d+`) is created, reviewed, and approved by the designated change-management authority. The ticket must remain open until the operation completes, and the ticket history must be retained for the audit period.”

If you later need to actually perform a rollback or scale in production, just provide the change-ticket ID and the revision number (for rollbacks) or the desired replica count (for scaling), and the system will enforce the ticket requirement automatically.
